Tax 25% (US parent, Australian operating subsidiaries). prepay.basis: Customer deposits of $143.9m at 30 Jun 2026 (10-Q, unattributed) — ESDS’s own filings describe an advance of ~INR 1,100–1,200 crore (~$130–140m) on the Sharon AI order, amortised monthly over the contract from go-live, and the ESDS Service Order calls for $140m of security; carried as the opening prepayment balance, credited over twenty quarters from Q4-26. The global-technology customer’s escrowed cash security was released on acceptance (8-K 20 Aug 2026) and Facility A of the GPU-backed loan is repaid from it (8-K 1 Oct 2026). Future contracts: the company’s stated policy is 10–20% of contract value as prepayment at signing, funding the GPU purchase order (10-K) — modelled at 20% of GPU capex on contracted capacity (~12% of contract value), credited evenly over the five-year term. NVIDIA pays no prepayment: the block’s ~$4bn of hardware is excluded from the prepayment base in the quarters it is paid (special.replaceG). Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry. Explicit opening-balance credits retain their own dated schedules. Mixed future tranches allocate inferred credits by contractual IT MW; purchase capex remains scheduled if delivery slips.

finance.wfMarginBasis: the quarterly waterfall runs at 60% EBITDA: the company guides to ~75% gross margin (Q2-26 printed 60.6% gross and 30.6% adjusted EBITDA on $1.9m of revenue), SemiAnalysis’s contract-level margins after colocation ($100/kW-month) and power ($0.05/kWh) are 88–91%, and Bloomberg consensus carries ~50% EBITDA in 2027 once corporate costs and the NVIDIA revenue share are charged; 60% sits between the tenant peers (CoreWeave 57–59%) and the company’s guide; the NVIDIA tranche rate is already net of NVIDIA’s share

Tranche B $206m fixed 9.95% with an 18-month make-whole; bullet at 42 months from first utilisation with an excess-cash sweep, DSRA, gross-LTV covenant on depreciated server cost; parent guarantee until Tranche A is repaid; Goldman Sachs and private-credit lenders, Jarden arranger; the “first in an expected series”), 20%/yr pool amortisation (GPU facilities sized to the five-year contracts and swept), $150m cash floor; lenders advance 80% of GPU cost on contracted capacity (SemiAnalysis sizes up to 80% LTC at 1.3× DSCR), 50% on spot; no shell capex — every site is leased colocation (non-cancellable operating leases, generally five-year terms, off balance sheet until service starts), rent inside EBITDA; 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $27 (the 19 Oct 2026 mark) plus the residual the flywheel cannot cover; notes: 212 MW secured, 120 MW contracted. Every megawatt is leased colocation: NEXTDC Melbourne and Sydney (87 MW, including the 72 MW NVIDIA site at M2), GreenSquareDC SYD1 (15 MW, 120-month term, online 19 Oct 2026), a New Zealand provider (14 MW, Q1 2027), other providers ~16 MW and 80 MW added on 20 August with no partner named.Q2-26 10-Q · 8-K 20 Aug · GreenSquareDC 19 Oct

The NVIDIA site lands in 2027. The amended and restated NEXTDC service order for 72 MW deploys in five phases from April to August 2027 and commits ~$623m over an undisclosed term; NEXTDC had 12 MW delivered and 60 MW of liquid-to-chip capacity under construction at M2 at 30 June. The company is “substantially dependent on NEXTDC”.10-Q commitments note · NEXTDC FY26 report

Beyond 212 MW is not modelled. Management speaks of a “gigawatt-scale” ambition across Australia, New Zealand and Asia-Pacific and says capacity is only announced with a customer and financing in place; the page stops at the secured footprint, and the signed-book-only scenario stops at 120 MW.8-K 1 Oct 2026 · Q2 call

64,600 GPUs by 2027Q3 on the contracted book — 40,000 GB300 for NVIDIA, 8,208 B300 for ESDS, ~7,000 in New Zealand, 5,776 for the global technology company, 2,048 for the AI platform, ~2,500 merchant. The company says 68,000+ by mid-2027; NVIDIA’s 9 Sep 2026 Australia release names Sharon AI at up to 68,000.8-Ks · June deck · 1 Oct release

Short book lives, long contracts. The accounting policy depreciates computer equipment over two to five years; management describes a 3–5 year contract plus two or more years of residual life. The refresh reserve here is a house allowance, not the accounting life.FY25 10-K · Q1-26 deck

Density is the company’s own. 40,000 GB300 on 72 MW is 556 per MW (~1.8 kW all-in); the ESDS cluster 547 per MW; the global-tech clusters 481. No filing states kW per GPU. The house 400 per MW used on the other pages would put ~30% more megawatts behind the same GPUs.8-K 12 Jun · Service Order No. 1 · June deck

Contract cohorts. The signed book keeps its filed all-in rate until expiry: ESDS $3.52, the global technology company $3.75, the AI platform $4.16, New Zealand $4.31 per GPU-hour — $15.8–18.9m per IT MW-year; management guides ~$15m per MW including storage. New capacity uses the shared house curve.

The NVIDIA block is a floor, not a price. Up to $4.88bn over six years on 40,000 GPUs is $2.32 per GPU-hour on average — NVIDIA’s maximum payment, which falls as capacity is sold to third parties; Sharon keeps the anchor price on capacity it sells and shares the spread above it at an undisclosed rate. The page carries $3.29 (owner ruling, 3 Aug 2026); the floor and a 40%-share placement are scenarios. No placement has printed, and reports of a pause in NVIDIA’s wider programme are unaddressed.8-K 12 Jun 2026 · NVIDIA Q2 FY27 10-Q · SemiAnalysis

Evidence. Contract dollars and terms are filed; the ESDS Service Order is public; GPU counts on two contracts are inferred; no customer is named except ESDS and NVIDIA. ESDS (CRISIL A-/Positive) has paid a ~$135m advance on its order but the $140m letter of credit the Service Order requires is not confirmed by either side; its go-live slipped from 16 Sep to early November.

Prepay, then borrow against the contract. Policy is 10–20% of contract value at signing to fund the purchase order; the inaugural $356m GPU-backed SPV facility (Tranche A $150m at 7.25% stepping to 9.95%, Tranche B $206m at 9.95%, 42-month bullet with a cash sweep) is “the first in an expected series”, with Tranche A repaid from the escrowed customer deposit on acceptance.10-K · Q2 deck · 8-K 1 Oct 2026 and facility agreement

$2.6bn raised in ten months. $103m pre-IPO notes (converted at $12.53), $74m from the TCDC sale, $125m IPO at $30 (Feb), $350m 6.00% converts (May), $900m of equity and pre-funded warrants at $68.73 plus $700m 4.75% converts (June), $356m of GPU debt (Sep). The USD.AI ($500m) and Digital Alpha ($200m) facilities remain undocumented and undrawn.10-Q · 8-Ks · S-1/A 20 Aug

The catch: $6.1bn of hardware is committed on the contracted book against $1.86bn of cash. At today’s price the residual equity in the model is raised at $27, against a June placement at $68.73 (Situational Awareness now holds 21.1% at a ~$65 cost); the converts (strikes $48.24 and $99.66) stay debt unless the price recovers.funding stack · summary table · 13D/A 17 Sep

Costs are rent and power. SemiAnalysis’s inputs — colocation $100 per kW-month, power $0.05/kWh — leave 88–91% contract-level margins; the NEXTDC 72 MW order implies $0.9–1.7m per MW-year depending on its undisclosed term; the company guides ~75% gross; consensus carries ~50% EBITDA in 2027 once overhead and the NVIDIA share are charged. The page runs 60%.SemiAnalysis · 10-Q · Bloomberg

Capex is $48–56m per MW on the filed commitments ($6.1bn on ~115 MW: NVIDIA ~$4bn for 72 MW including networking, storage and the VAST layer; New Zealand $765m for 14 MW; ESDS $720m for 15 MW) against a $39m per MW management guide. No shell: the landlord’s capital sits in the rent.10-Q · Q2 deck · Q1 call

Maintenance, not replacement. Tray swap at 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares — the same house allowance as the other pages — on a five-year take-or-pay book that recovers the hardware inside the term at these rates (gross payback 2.1–2.9 years on the customer clusters, 4.9 at the NVIDIA floor).model · research pack

Some equity, not none. Base: 10% of the 2027–28 build plus whatever the prepayments, the GPU facilities and operating cash cannot cover, issued at $27 — the bridge shows the count. The June placement was at $68.73; the price has since fallen by more than half, with a 52% drop between 6 and 23 October on no filing.8-K 17 Jun 2026 · Finnhub

The NVIDIA economics are the swing. Floor versus placement moves the 72 MW block between $2.32 and $3.49 per GPU-hour; every $1 per GPU-hour on the block is ~$175m a year retained. The signed-book-only scenario shows what the 120 MW contracted today is worth on its own.scenarios · SemiAnalysis
EPS is the long-run anchor. Pick your multiple.after the raise

market.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
market.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
market.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

market.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.
